record.vts_boundary_basis: MSC.389(94) (Z3-S1), the IMO instrument for VRS-0022, names Chengshan Jiao VTS Centre (Weihai MSA) as the shore authority for the 24 nm reporting area, states the Centre has radar and a continuous 24-hour watch and provides traffic information to participating ships, requires a listening watch on the VTS working channel, and requires ships NUC or at anchor 'in the TSSs' to report to VTS. COLREG.2/Circ.66 (Z3-S2) cross-refers the TSS to the SRS. VTS extent is therefore taken from the IMO instrument's 24 nm area; no separate national VTS area description (Chinese VTS rules for Chengshan Jiao) was located. The inner TSS vertices lie 3.1 to 15.1 nm from the Centre.
record.reporting_authority: Weihai Maritime Safety Administration; reports to Chengshan Jiao VTS Centre (VHF 08, secondary 09 or 65)
record.reporting_boundary_basis: SRS area is the 24 nm circle centred on the VTS Centre (MSC.389(94) para 2.1). All vertices of the inner TSS (points 1-9, 13-15, 26-27) lie between 3.1 and 15.1 nm from the circle centre, so the whole scheme lies inside the 24 nm area. Participation: passenger ships; oil tankers 150 GT and above and ships carrying hazardous cargo; LOA over 200 m or draught over 12 m; towing/pushing vessels; ships NUC, at anchor in the TSSs, RAM or with defective navigational equipment.
record.evidence_summary: IMO Part I system VRS-0022 (MSC.389(94), in force 1 June 2015) covers a 24 nm circle around Chengshan Jiao VTS Centre; the TSS coordinates in COLREG.2/Circ.66 were measured against that circle. All vertices of the inner TSS (points 1-9, 13-15, 26-27) lie between 3.1 and 15.1 nm from the circle centre, so the whole scheme lies inside the 24 nm area. The same IMO instrument establishes the VTS Centre as operating the system with radar and 24-hour watch.

record.vts_boundary_basis: No VTS established. The IMO instruments name MRCC Las Palmas (Salvamento Marítimo) only as a Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre receiving CANREP reports and voluntary TSS notifications (Z3-S3, Z3-S4). An official press release (Z3-S9) says CCS Las Palmas carries out traffic monitoring, and a media report (Z3-S10) says the CCS 'controlled' ships transiting the TSS, but no official source was found that designates a VTS or defines a VTS area covering the TSS. The Las Palmas / Santa Cruz de Tenerife port VTS cover port waters only (not checked in detail; lead only).
record.reporting_scheme_name: CANREP (Mandatory ship reporting system for the Canary Islands)
record.reporting_authority: Salvamento Marítimo: MRCC Las Palmas (entry east of 015°30'W) / MRCC Tenerife (entry west of 015°30'W)
record.reporting_boundary_basis: CANREP area is a polygon (points A-N) along the outer limit of the territorial sea around the archipelago (MSC.213(81) para 2.1). Plotting the COLREG.2/Circ.57 coordinates shows all Eastern TSS points inside the polygon; its northern termination (points 3 and 11-12 at about 28°20'N, on the line CANREP D-E) lies on the CANREP boundary line within 0.05', and the polygon vertex used for the TSS's inshore traffic zone coincides with a CANREP vertex, so the TSS lies within the reporting area. Applies only to tankers of 600 dwt and above carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil, bitumen or tar.
record.voluntary_reporting: Yes: voluntary notification of entry to and departure from the TSS via MRCC Las Palmas, VHF channel 16 (COLREG.2/Circ.57 note)
record.evidence_summary: Inside VRS-0023 CANREP (MSC.213(81), in force 1 Dec 2006) by coordinate check; mandatory only for heavy-grade oil tankers of 600 dwt and above. MRCC Las Palmas is an MRCC, not a designated VTS; traffic monitoring of the TSS by Salvamento Marítimo is reported but no VTS designation or VTS area was found.
record.source_date: MSC.213(81) adopted 12 May 2006, in force 1 Dec 2006; COLREG.2/Circ.57 26 May 2006, implemented 1 Dec 2006; press release 20 Nov 2020; media 2 Feb 2024; accessed 29 Sep 2026
record.unresolved_issue: Salvamento Marítimo website unavailable (TLS/503), so its own description of CCS functions and any Spanish designation of a coastal VTS for the Canary TSS could not be checked; ALRS Vol 6 not consulted. CANREP chartlet not inspected (coordinate check used instead).
record.vts_leads: MRCC Las Palmas / CCS (Salvamento Marítimo) traffic monitoring of the TSS (not a designated VTS on the evidence found)
record.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: MRS only (CANREP); inclusion now checked by plotting TSS coordinates against the CANREP polygon

record.vts_boundary_basis: No VTS established. The IMO instruments name MRCC Tenerife (Salvamento Marítimo) only as a Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre receiving CANREP reports and voluntary TSS notifications (Z3-S3, Z3-S4). An official press release (Z3-S9) says CCS Las Palmas carries out traffic monitoring, and a media report (Z3-S10) says the CCS 'controlled' ships transiting the TSS, but no official source was found that designates a VTS or defines a VTS area covering the TSS. The Las Palmas / Santa Cruz de Tenerife port VTS cover port waters only (not checked in detail; lead only).
record.reporting_scheme_name: CANREP (Mandatory ship reporting system for the Canary Islands)
record.reporting_authority: Salvamento Marítimo: MRCC Las Palmas (entry east of 015°30'W) / MRCC Tenerife (entry west of 015°30'W)
record.reporting_boundary_basis: CANREP area is a polygon (points A-N) along the outer limit of the territorial sea around the archipelago (MSC.213(81) para 2.1). Plotting the COLREG.2/Circ.57 coordinates shows all Western TSS points inside the polygon; its northern termination (points 3 and 19 at about 28°34'-28°38'N, on the line CANREP C-D) lies on the CANREP boundary line within 0.05', and the polygon vertex used for the TSS's inshore traffic zone coincides with a CANREP vertex, so the TSS lies within the reporting area. Applies only to tankers of 600 dwt and above carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil, bitumen or tar.
record.voluntary_reporting: Yes: voluntary notification of entry to and departure from the TSS via MRCC Tenerife, VHF channel 16 (COLREG.2/Circ.57 note)
record.evidence_summary: Inside VRS-0023 CANREP (MSC.213(81), in force 1 Dec 2006) by coordinate check; mandatory only for heavy-grade oil tankers of 600 dwt and above. MRCC Tenerife is an MRCC, not a designated VTS; traffic monitoring of the TSS by Salvamento Marítimo is reported but no VTS designation or VTS area was found.
record.source_date: MSC.213(81) adopted 12 May 2006, in force 1 Dec 2006; COLREG.2/Circ.57 26 May 2006, implemented 1 Dec 2006; press release 20 Nov 2020; media 2 Feb 2024; accessed 29 Sep 2026
record.unresolved_issue: Salvamento Marítimo website unavailable (TLS/503), so its own description of CCS functions and any Spanish designation of a coastal VTS for the Canary TSS could not be checked; ALRS Vol 6 not consulted. CANREP chartlet not inspected (coordinate check used instead).
record.vts_leads: MRCC Tenerife / CCS (Salvamento Marítimo) traffic monitoring of the TSS (not a designated VTS on the evidence found)
record.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: MRS only (CANREP); inclusion now checked by plotting TSS coordinates against the CANREP polygon
